newsitem.title: USA: Clinton expected to name Weld envoy to Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expected to name Weld envoy to Mexico.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is expected to name Massachusetts Gov. William Weld, a possible spoiler of Vice President Al Gore's presidential hopes, to be ambassador to Mexico, an administration official said on Friday.
Weld, a moderate Republican touted as a potential Republican presidential nominee in 2000, would replace former American Stock Exchange President James Jones in the sensitive diplomatic post.
The official, who asked not to be identified, said Weld's nomination was not ready to be announced but the governor was Clinton's choice to be ambassador to Mexico.
Weld was vacationing in Virginia and unable to comment, but his press spokesman said he would be honored to be considered for the post.

"President Clinton has worked closely with Governor Weld over many years and has high regard for him," said White House spokesman Mike McCurry. "I personally think it would be a dandy choice," he added.

Weld, who speaks Spanish fluently, last worked in Washington as an assistant attorney general in charge of the criminal division at the Justice Department, with an emphasis on narcotics and public corruption. He left in 1988 after two years.

Now nearing the end of his second term as governor, Weld lost a close race to replace Democrat John Kerry in the Senate in 1996. He said several years ago that he would leave the Massachusetts statehouse after two terms, but has more recently toyed with the idea of running for a third term.

"Two terms is enough. After that, I just want to go back to the private practice of law," said Weld, who quietly made his interest in joining the Clinton Cabinet known during the second term administration reshuffle in late 1996.

Weld's exit from the governor's office would heighten a race to succeed him that is already under way even though the next election is not until November 1998. Lt. Gov. Paul Cellucci and State Treasurer Joseph Malone are rivals for the Republican nomination, while Rep. Joseph Kennedy is the presumptive favorite for the Democratic nomination.

Kennedy, son of the late Sen. Robert Kennedy and a popular member of the Kennedy political dynasty in Massachusetts, might face competition from Attorney General Scott Harshbarger for the Democratic nomination.
A further possibility in the potential round of musical chairs is the expected return of former Democratic Mayor Ray Flynn to the Boston political scene.
Administration sources said Lindy Boggs, a former Democratic congresswoman from Louisiana, was Clinton's first choice to succeed Flynn as U.S. ambassador to the Vatican.
